prompt: Two teachers compare final exam scores. A random sample from Class A has mean $\bar{x}_A = 82.4$; a random sample from Class B has mean $\bar{x}_B = 78.9$. What is the point estimate for $\mu_A - \mu_B$?
hint: A point estimate is a single best guess for a parameter. What sample quantity naturally estimates a difference of two population means?

hints.text: A point estimate is a single best guess for a parameter. What sample quantity naturally estimates a difference of two population means?
Use the difference of the sample means in the same order as the parameter, A minus B: $82.4 - 78.9$.
$82.4 - 78.9 = 3.5$, so the point estimate is $3.5$ points.

explanation: The parameter is $\mu_A - \mu_B$, and each population mean is estimated by its sample mean, so the point estimate is $\bar{x}_A - \bar{x}_B$.
Subtracting in the order A minus B gives $82.4 - 78.9 = 3.5$.
The point estimate is $3.5$ points. Whether that gap is statistically significant depends on the spreads and sample sizes.

alternativeExplanations.title: Order matters
steps: If you had defined the parameter as $\mu_B - \mu_A$, the estimate would be $-3.5$.
Always subtract in the same order as the parameter you wrote down.
Here it is A minus B: $+3.5$.
